content: coffee A controlled blast on a movie set close to the O2 venue in London ignited a fire that consumed a van and caused damage to a car and a lorry. Firefighters were dispatched to an open‑air storage area on Dock Road in Silvertown just before eight o’clock on Saturday evening. After roughly an hour, the flames were brought under control by a crew of about twenty‑five rescuers, with nobody hurt. Authorities said the incident stemmed from a pre‑arranged shooting activity near the arena, which is slated to host performances by Niall Horan and the band Texas in the coming days. The London Fire Brigade updated its social‑media account on Saturday night, noting that the blaze in the Silvertown yard is now contained, that one vehicle was destroyed while most of another car and a lorry suffered damage, and that no injuries have been reported. It added that the fire originated from a controlled explosion on the set that escaped containment, that emergency teams acted swiftly to put it out, and that personnel will stay on site for the rest of the evening. The yard lies near the Thames‑crossing cable car link, and a Metropolitan Police spokesman confirmed they are investigating reports of explosions heard around the O2 in Greenwich.
